title: Architecture Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (Consolidated ADRs)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. It also summarizes the active ADRs that shape those standards. The goal is to provide a single reference for architects, on-call engineers, and product teams when designing or modifying services that interact with the inference platform.

Intended audience
- Service owners and architects
- Backend and platform engineers
- SRE and reliability engineers
- Applied ML and model-onboarding teams

Table of contents
1. API standards
2. Coding standards
3. Infrastructure standards (IaC & networking)
4. Model-serving standards
5. Observability standards
6. Performance SLOs and benchmarking
7. Key ADRs (summary and links)
8. Ownership and rollout checklist

---

1) API standards

Purpose: Ensure consistent, discoverable, and stable HTTP APIs across Redwood services that integrate with the Redwood runtime and customer-facing APIs.

Principles
- Design for clients: clear resources and predictable behavior.
- Stability first: contract changes should be backward compatible or follow a documented deprecation flow.
- Observable: every API must emit request/response metadata required for tracing and cost attribution.

Conventions
- Base path and versioning: /api/v{major}/{service}/...; bump MAJOR for breaking changes only.
- Resource naming: nouns (e.g., /models, /deployments); use plural forms.
- HTTP methods: GET for reads, POST for actions/creates, PUT/PATCH for updates, DELETE for deletes.
- Idempotency: POST endpoints that create resources must accept an Idempotency-Key header to prevent duplicate work.
- Pagination: cursor-based pagination using parameters 'page_token' and 'page_size'.
- Rate limiting headers: include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset on responses when applicable.
- Error model: consistent error schema: {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional list}. Use 4xx for client errors, 5xx for server errors. Provide machine-readable retryable flag when applicable.

Security
- All internal APIs must enforce mTLS where traffic crosses trust boundaries; customer-facing APIs use TLS + token auth.
- Sensitive fields (PII, secrets) must be redacted from logs and traces.

Examples
- Model metadata: GET /api/v1/models/{model_id} -> 200 { id, name, version, quantization_profile, supported_sequences }
- Inference request: POST /api/v1/infer with JSON body: {"model_id": "rwd-bert-1", "input": "...", "options": {...} }

Change/Deprecation process
1. Create ADR describing rationale and migration path.
2. Announce to platform-consumers and include migration guide.
3. Maintain old version for minimum 90 days or negotiated SLAs.

---

2) Coding standards

Purpose: Maintain code quality, readability, and fast onboarding across services.

Languages and frameworks
- Primary backend languages: Go (server-side services), Python (ML tooling, lightweight microservices), and TypeScript (web and API gateways).
- Use gRPC for high-throughput internal RPCs; REST/JSON for external-facing endpoints.

Linting and formatting
- Go: gofmt + golangci-lint with standard rule set.
- Python: Black + ruff + mypy for typed modules. All new Python services should use type annotations for public functions.
- TypeScript: Prettier + ESLint with AirBnB rules (adapted).

Testing and CI
- Unit tests must run on every PR. Coverage target: >= 60% for service code, 80% for critical runtime helpers.
- Integration tests must run in CI for changes that touch infra contracts (e.g., messages, DB migrations).
- Benchmark tests: performance-sensitive code must include a benchmark harness that can run in CI and locally.

Commit & PR guidelines
- Commit messages: <area>: short summary (e.g., runtime: fix cache eviction). Include ticket id.
- PR size: prefer small, reviewable PRs. Large PRs require a design doc and pairing review.

Dependency management
- Use deterministic dependency files (go.sum, poetry.lock, package-lock.json).
- Monthly dependency update cadence; security updates as fast as possible.

Secrets and keys
- No secrets in repos. Use org secret manager (Vault/Secrets Manager) and reference via configuration.

---

3) Infrastructure standards (IaC & networking)

Principles
- All infra is declared in Terraform modules under the central repo unless a documented exception exists.
- Environments: dev, staging, prod with separate state and accounts projects.
- Immutable infra: prefer replacing instances over in-place patches for critical services.

Terraform module conventions (table)
| Module | Purpose | Required tags | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rwd-network | VPC, subnets, peering | env, team, cost-center | eng-infra | Standard CIDR allocations; enable flow logs |
| rwd-gke | Kubernetes clusters | env, team, kube-version | eng-platform | Cluster autoscaling defaults defined |
| rwd-gpu-pool | GPU node pools | env, team, gpu-type | eng-infra | Reserved capacity for Dedicated customers |

Networking & security
- Use private connectivity (VPC peering/VPN) for all cross-account traffic.
- Egress control: only allow required outbound destinations; default deny otherwise.
- KMS usage mandatory for customer keys and secrets.

Operational controls
- Tagging: 'env', 'team', 'service', 'cost-center' required on all cloud resources.
- Terraform plans must be reviewed and approved (policy as code checks via Sentinel/OPA).
- Resource quotas and budget alerts configured per environment.

---

4) Model-serving standards

Purpose: Ensure model deployments are predictable in latency, cost, and reliability and compatible with Redwood Serving runtime.

Model contract
- Models must include metadata: model_id, semantic_version (semver), framework (e.g., pytorch, tflite), signature (input/output schema), max_sequence_length, kv_cache_support (true/false), quantization_profiles (list).
- Provide a small validation script that runs a smoke inference and verifies outputs match expected shape.

Versioning & rollouts
- Semantic versioning for model artifacts. Deployments reference model_id + version.
- Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over at least 24 hours with automated quality checks (perf + quality).

Resource profiles and runtime config (table)
| Class | Typical GPU | Batch size (default) | Latency SLO (p95) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| small-llm | A10G | 32 | 200ms | short sequences, embeddings-heavy |
| medium-llm | A100-40GB | 16 | 350ms | balanced throughput/latency |
| large-llm | H100-80GB | 8 | 600ms | long-context models, KV-cache intensive |

Quantization & precision
- Production variants must include at least one quantized profile (e.g., int8, int4) with regression tests against baseline FP16 outputs.

Routing & fallback
- Smart routing policy: route by latency target -> cost tier -> region.
- Automatic fallback chain: model variant -> cheaper quantized variant -> regional replica -> degraded mode returning a cached response/shorter output when available.

Batching and caching
- Default continuous batching enabled on runtime with adaptive batch window up to 50ms for latency-sensitive models.
- Prefix & KV caching supported; services must declare cache keys for deterministic inference where applicable.

Observability for models
- Emit per-request model_id, model_version, variant, seq_length, tokens_in/tokens_out, and cost_estimate metric.
- Maintain per-model quality metrics: eval-set accuracy/Al score + drift windows.

---

5) Observability standards

Metrics
- Metric namespaces: rwd.<domain>.<service>.<metric>. Use clear suffixes: _count, _latency_ms, _error_count.
- Required metrics for services interacting with runtime: request_count, request_errors, request_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, tokens_consumed_total.
- Export to Prometheus with reasonable scrape intervals (15s).

Tracing & logs
- Distributed tracing: OpenTelemetry with 128-bit trace IDs; sample at 1% by default, 100% for errors.
- Logs: structured JSON with keys: timestamp, level, service, request_id, trace_id, user_id (if applicable), message. PII redaction required.

Dashboards & alerts
- Every critical service has a standard dashboard template: Overview, Latency, Errors, Throughput, Cost.
- Alerting thresholds (example):
  - Service error rate > 1% sustained for 5m -> P1 on-call page.
  - p95 latency > SLO * 1.5 for 10m -> P1.
  - tokens_consumed_total anomalous spike (statistical alarm) -> P2.

Logging retention
- Short-term: full logs 30 days; Long-term: aggregated events/alerts 365 days. Additional retention negotiable for enterprise customers as part of add-on.

---

6) Performance SLOs, benchmarking and validation

System-level SLOs (examples)
- Hosted inference API: availability 99.95% (monthly).
- Per-request latency SLOs by model class (see model-serving table above).
- Tail-latency objective: p99 should be < 3x p95 for steady-state workloads.

Benchmarking harness
- Every change affecting runtime or model-serving must run the benchmark suite:
  1. Latency microbench (single-client, warm cache)
  2. Throughput stress (concurrent clients, mixed prompt lengths)
  3. Cold-start / model-load tests for new artifacts
- Benchmarks must be reproducible with the provided harness (bench/ directory) and use standardized datasets/prompts.

Performance regression process
1. CI detects regression (>=5% regression in p95 latency or throughput drop).
2. Fail gating; notify owners with artifact and diff.
3. Reproduce locally with trace-level logs.
4. If regression confirmed, rollback or apply mitigation (e.g., widen batch window, change kernel selection).

---

7) Key ADRs (summary)

- ADR-2024-07: "Adopt semantic model versioning and rollout policy" — rationale: decouple model development from deployments; consequence: model deployments reference explicit versions and enable safe canarying.
- ADR-2025-02: "Default to continuous batching with adaptive windows" — rationale: substantial cost savings with limited latency impact; consequence: runtime must provide per-model batch window overrides.
- ADR-2025-08: "Unified API versioning scheme (/api/v{major})" — rationale: simplify client compatibility.
- ADR-2026-01: "Quantized variants required for production models" — rationale: control unit economics; consequence: onboarding checklist includes quantization profile and regression tests.

Each ADR above has a full text page linked in related_pages. When proposing a new ADR, follow the ADR template: context, decision, trade-offs, alternatives considered, and migration plan.

---

8) Ownership, rollout checklist, and exceptions

Ownership
- Standards steward: Architecture Guild (contact: arch-guild@redwood.ai).
- Service owner: defined in service metadata and on the service registry.
- SRE & observability: eng-sre team for alert tuning and incident postmortems.

Rollout checklist for adopting these standards
1. Read relevant ADRs and ensure design aligns with principles.
2. Create implementation proposal (1-2 pages).
3. Run CI + benchmark harness; add required metrics and traces.
4. Submit PR with terraform plan and module references if infra changes required.
5. Execute canary rollout and monitor quality metrics for at least 24 hours.
6. Announce GA and update service registry and runbooks.

Exceptions
- Exceptions must be documented in a short RFC and approved by Architecture Guild. Timeboxed exceptions expire after 90 days unless renewed.

Appendix A: Example API error schema (JSON)
{
  "code": "MODEL_NOT_FOUND",
  "message": "Model with id rwd-bert-1 not found",
  "details": [{"field":"model_id","message":"invalid or missing"}],
  "retryable": false
}

Appendix B: Quick Terraform policy example (YAML)
policies:
  - name: require-tags
    condition: contains(all(resource.tags), ["env","team","service","cost-center"])
    action: deny

Appendix C: Contact & escalation
- Architecture Guild: arch-guild@redwood.ai
- On-call SRE: see team rota (internal link)
- Security exceptions: security@redwood.ai
